title: LiveStarPro: Proactive Streaming Video Understanding with Hierarchical Memory for Long-Horizon Streams
title_zh: LiveStarPro：面向长时程视频流的层次化记忆主动式流媒体视频理解
abstract_en: Despite the remarkable progress of Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs), current online architectures still struggle to simultaneously process continuous video streams, decide autonomously when to respond, and preserve long-horizon contextual memory. These obstacles undermine real-time responsiveness and cause severe forgetting throughout prolonged interactions. In this work, we introduce LiveStarPro, a live streaming assistant that is designed for proactive video understanding over long-horizon streams. The design of LiveStarPro rests on three complementary components. The first component is Streaming Verification Decoding (SVeD), an inference framework that identifies the appropriate response timing through single-pass perplexity verification, thereby eliminating the dependency on explicit silence tokens. The second component is Streaming Causal Attention Masks (SCAM), a training strategy that enforces incremental video-language alignment over variable-length streams. The third component is Tree-Structured Hierarchical Memory (TSHM), a recursive memory architecture that organizes evicted historical information into event chains and consequently enables efficient retrieval from effectively unbounded video streams. To facilitate a comprehensive evaluation under realistic online conditions, we further present OmniStarPro, a large-scale benchmark that spans 15 diverse real-world scenarios and that extends to hour-scale streams for the assessment of long-term recall. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LiveStarPro consistently surpasses existing methods, attaining a 28.9% improvement in semantic correctness and an 18.2% reduction in timing error, while its streaming key-value cache further yields a 1.58x inference speedup over the same model without caching. The model and the code are publicly available at https://github.com/sotayang/LiveStarPro.
abstract_zh: 尽管 Video Large Language Models（Video-LLMs）取得了显著进展，现有在线架构仍难以同时处理连续视频流、自主判断何时响应，并保持长时程上下文记忆。这会削弱实时交互能力，并在长时间交互中导致严重遗忘。本文提出 LiveStarPro，一个面向长时程视频流主动理解的实时流媒体助手。其核心由三部分组成：Streaming Verification Decoding（SVeD）通过单次 perplexity 验证判断合适响应时机，避免依赖显式 silence token；Streaming Causal Attention Masks（SCAM）作为训练策略，在可变长度视频流中强制进行增量式视频-语言对齐；Tree-Structured Hierarchical Memory（TSHM）将被移出上下文窗口的历史信息递归组织为事件链，从而支持对近乎无限长度视频流的高效检索。为在真实在线条件下进行全面评估，作者还提出 OmniStarPro，一个覆盖 15 类真实场景、扩展到小时级视频流的大规模 benchmark，用于评测长期记忆与回忆能力。实验表明，LiveStarPro 稳定优于现有方法，语义正确性提升 28.9%，响应时机误差降低 18.2%，并且其 streaming key-value cache 相比无缓存版本带来 1.58 倍推理加速。
key_points_zh: 提出 LiveStarPro，面向连续、长时程视频流的主动式 Video-LLM 助手，重点解决实时响应、自主发话时机与长期上下文保持问题。
设计 Streaming Verification Decoding（SVeD），用单次 perplexity 验证判断是否应响应，避免传统在线模型对 silence token 或显式静默标记的依赖。
提出 Streaming Causal Attention Masks（SCAM），在训练阶段约束模型进行增量式视频-语言对齐，使其更适配可变长度在线视频流。
引入 Tree-Structured Hierarchical Memory（TSHM），将历史信息组织为树状事件链，实现对超长视频流中被驱逐上下文的高效检索与长期回忆。
构建 OmniStarPro benchmark，覆盖 15 个真实场景和小时级流媒体评测；实验显示 LiveStarPro 在语义正确性、响应时机与推理速度上均优于现有方法。

llm_assessment.comment: A highly relevant streaming video-agent paper with proactive response timing, long-horizon memory, latency-aware design, and reusable online evaluation.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这是一篇高度契合实时视频智能体方向的工作，结合了主动响应时机、长时记忆、低延迟设计和可复用在线评测。
